newsitem.title: USA: Fed added via overnight system RPs, bill pass eyed.
newsitem.headline: Fed added via overnight system RPs, bill pass eyed.

text.p: The Federal Reserve added reserves to the banking system via a round of overnight system repurchase agreements Wednesday, the New York Fed confirmed.

The operation came an hour earlier than usual, although the Fed declined to say why. Analysts said federal funds were under pressure and waiting the extra hour wouldn't insure the Fed would receive the necessary collateral from dealers.
Fed funds were trading at 5-9/16 percent when the Fed entered the open market, well above the 5-1/4 percent target rate.
Analysts still expct a bill pass later this session.
Fed action this session was no surprise, since the Fed faced at least a $5 billion add need in the reserve period ending Wednesday, and the Fed stayed on the sidelines Monday and Tuesday.
The early operation was the third in the past week and a half.
Meanwhile, with the add need seen rising substantially in the new reserve period, analysts expect a bill pass, which adds permanent reserves to the banking system, as early as this session.
